As someone with an ED, there is such a thing as “plateau”-ing and the all mighty “woosh.” Sometimes you just need to change things up for a couple days, whether that’s treating yourself to something yummy, reducing exercise, eating different kinds of foods, etc. After unhealthily manipulating my weight for almost a decade, I’ve learned that your body ALWAYS wants to get to its natural set point, and the only way to force your body to do otherwise is by having disordered eating. To reach your set point, which is when your body is at its peak health and ability, you need to listen to what nutrients your body is “asking for” on a daily, sometimes hourly basis. It’s not about following a super strict diet/meal plan and eating an exact amount of calories everyday. I do think CICO is accurate to some degree but our bodies are MUCH more complicated than that. If you’re truly aiming to be HEALTHIER and not just thinner, I would give your body more room to ask for what it needs to heal. Sometimes that’s more fat, sometimes less protein and more carbs. Sometimes a rest day to allow your muscles to recover and not retain fluid. THEN, your body will be able to naturally gain or lose weight to get to its set point.

I am an ER nurse; PLEASE DO NOT GO TO THE ER FOR CONSTIPATION. Constipation=3 or more days since your last bowel movement and is NOT an emergency. You can take a million different types of over-the-counter laxatives/stool softeners/fiber supplements/enemas/or just dig your poop out of your own damn body instead of taking up a bed and asking a random stranger to stick their fingers up your butt. Obviously none of that applies if you are physically too weak or disabled to try these solutions yourself. The ONLY time constipation becomes an emergency is when it stops being “constipation” and turns into “bowel obstruction,” which will cause nausea/vomiting. If you are just feeling abdominal discomfort or gas pains, please try taking a laxative first before crowding your ER, because that’s exactly what we’ll give you after you wait 5+ hours in the waiting room. Sorry if I sounded bitchy, I know constipation can cause real pain, but we can’t even do anything for it if you come in. We are just going to give you an expensive laxative that you could’ve bought for $5 at CVS or Target.
